questionsToConsider: Is this for a pub night, a team social or a classroom? A mixed crowd needs questions from several subjects so nobody dominates.
Should a wrong pick in the fruit question cost a point, or would that feel harsh for your players?
Will teams play together on one phone, or will everyone answer on their own device?
Do you need the tiebreaker at all, or is a shared win fine for your group?
guide.howToUseResponses: Sort the responses by score to find the winner, then use the tiebreaker to settle any draw: the guess closest to 88 takes it. Look at which question most people got wrong before your next quiz. If nearly everyone missed it, keep it as a showstopper; if the wording confused people, rewrite it.
customizeSteps: Swap in questions on your own theme, keeping one point on each correct option and a minus point on wrong picks in any pick-all question.
Move the score bands if you change the number of questions, so the champion result still needs nearly every answer right.
Share the link on screen or in your group chat, and read the scoreboard in the dashboard when the round closes.

faqs.q: How many questions should a trivia quiz have?
faqs.a: For a single round played on phones, eight to twelve questions keeps it quick. A full quiz night usually runs several rounds of that size with a break between them.

faqs.q: How do I handle a tie in a trivia quiz?
faqs.a: Use a closest-guess number question that is not scored. This template asks how many keys a piano has, and the nearest guess to 88 wins.

faqs.q: What makes a good trivia question?
faqs.a: One clear right answer, wrong options that sound plausible, and a fact people enjoy learning even when they miss it.

faqs.q: Can teams play this trivia quiz together?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask for a team name on the first question and have one person answer for the table.

blocks.title: Trivia time. Eight questions from all over the map, one tiebreaker, and your result at the end.
What name or team name should go on the scoreboard?
How many hearts does an octopus have?
What is the hardest natural substance on Earth?
Botanically speaking, which of these are fruits? Pick all that apply.
blocks.description: A wrong pick costs a point, so only choose the ones you're sure of.

blocks.title: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
True or false: lightning never strikes the same place twice.
In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
Tiebreaker: how many keys are there on a standard piano?
blocks.description: Not scored. If two players draw, the closest guess wins.

endings.title: Warm-up round 🎲
endings.bodyMd: Trivia rewards odd facts, and now you have eight new ones. Octopuses have three hearts, by the way. Have another go.

endings.title: Quiz night champion 🏆
endings.bodyMd: Almost a clean sweep. The botanical fruits and the lightning myth are where most players slip, and you got through.

endings.title: Strong contender 💡
endings.bodyMd: A good score with a couple of traps along the way. The octopus and the lightning question catch plenty of people out.
